title: The Quiet Power of Reading Slowly

paragraphs.text: In an age of endless scrolling, the ability to read a single long article from beginning to end has become something of a rare skill. Attention, it turns out, is not merely a fixed resource but a muscle that strengthens or withers with use.

Slow reading—the deliberate, unhurried engagement with a text—confers benefits that skimming cannot. It allows the reader to trace an argument's architecture, to notice the rhythm of a sentence, and to weigh evidence rather than merely absorb conclusions.

For language learners, this habit is doubly valuable. Encountering unfamiliar words in rich context fixes them in memory far more effectively than isolated memorisation. Each re-reading of a difficult passage quietly expands the boundaries of comprehension.

The challenge is not intellectual but habitual. Set a timer for twenty minutes, silence your phone, and read without interruption. The reward is a mind that can hold a thought long enough to truly understand it.
